A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Internal Confidence study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching across the reorganization. V1's appendix is explicitly a placeholder.

before.justification: V1 reports original uncertainty-estimation results across three models and datasets in Table 1, plus RAG and model-cascading experiments in Figure 4.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and adaptive-inference results, alongside new runtime comparisons in Tables 2 and A1 and demonstration-count experiments in Figure A2.

M1.justification: V1 Section 4.2 and v2 Section 3.2 retain the same single-pass Yes/No scoring, weighted aggregation across layers and tokens, fixed final-layer/final-token decision center, and attenuated weights. Expanded explanations and revised notation do not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TriviaQA, SciQ, and GSM8K, plus TriviaQA-based RAG and model cascading. The added timing and demonstration-count experiments use this existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds direct post-generation comparisons against Perplexity, Semantic Entropy, P(TRUE), Lexical Similarity, and SAR in Tables 2 and A1. Table 1 retains its original comparator membership: P(YES) (top right) and P(YES) (naive avg) match the earlier P(Yes) and naive-average variant.

E3.justification: V1 specifies one positive/negative demonstration pair for every model; v2 specifies zero-shot prompting for Llama/Qwen and three-shot prompting for Phi. V2 also adds runtime/speedup measurements, RAG timing, and controlled demonstration-count and answer-length analyses. Greedy decoding, answer-correctness criteria, and AUC/PRR/ECE remain unchanged. Newly disclosed sample counts do not establish revised splits.

E4.justification: V2 adds a demonstration-dependence study varying one to five positive/negative example pairs (Figure A2) and an analysis of runtime scaling with answer length (Figure 4). These test previously unexamined dependencies. The earlier confidence histograms and locality curves are retained as Figures A1 and A3, rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its comparisons. The new experiments retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces many self-evaluation results under changed reported prompting: Qwen's Internal Confidence average AUC changes from 65.6 to 67.1 and PRR from 32.5 to 31.7. New Table 2 reports GSM8K AUC/time of 66.8/0.3 seconds for Internal Confidence versus 65.7/180.6 seconds for SAR. Table A1 reports faster Internal Confidence but lower AUC than most answer-level comparators on TriviaQA and SciQ.

T1.justification: The knowledge-boundary definition and scoring, aggregation, decay, and locality equations retain their mathematical substance. Renaming w to alpha and relocating baseline formulas to Appendix B are notation and presentation changes. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: V2 extends the headline efficiency claim to explicit runtime superiority over answer-level uncertainty estimators in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The original query-level uncertainty concept, training-free method contribution, and cost-saving RAG/cascading claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly qualifies greedy-decoding correctness as a heuristic that may miss capabilities accessible through other decoding strategies (Section 3.1). Appendix A.1 expands caveats about residual ambiguity and difficulty separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty. Appendix C also adds interpretations of demonstration dependence and retained confidence distributions.

D1.justification: V2 first specifies 10,000 TriviaQA, 10,000 SciQ, and 5,000 GSM8K samples, reserving 1,000 per dataset for validation. It also documents random positive/negative demonstration selection for the new sensitivity study. These improve experimental documentation; the code repository remains the same.

R1.justification: V2 adds supporting literature on linear probes, factual-confidence estimators, agentic computation costs, internal representations, and uncertainty disentanglement. Examples include Alain and Bengio, Mahaut et al., and Mucsanyi et al. Its central positioning relative to trained probes and abstention methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively edits the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and discussion. It moves the preliminary concepts to Appendix A and detailed baseline descriptions to Appendix B, reorganizes the experimental narrative, and adds substantive appendix sections. Authorship and conference-header text also change.

P2.justification: V2 switches from two columns to a single-column conference layout, adds runtime scatter/bar plots and Tables 2/A1, and redraws adaptive-inference figures with baseline reference lines. V1 Figures 3 and 5 move intact to v2 Figures A1 and A3; the new Figure 5 additionally displays locality results averaged across datasets.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful direct timing evidence beyond v1's call fractions, tests demonstration dependence, and clarifies decoding and ambiguity limitations. The gain is limited by missing hardware and timing-protocol details and the retained calibration overclaim: in v2 Table 1, Phi's average ECE is 12.7 for Internal Confidence versus 7.5 for P(YES).
